values.note: $35 a night; $600 a month; $2,000 for the season (May 1 - Oct 1, paid in advance at City Hall). Tents on a site pay the same. Read 2026-11-11.

fees.source: https://cityofmountainlakemn.gov/business/island-view-campground/ ('Standard Rate is $35/night.'; 'A discounted monthly rate of $600 is available.'; 'A discounted seasonal rate of $2,000 is available.'; 'Tenting on a site also allowed – same rates apply'), read 2026-11-11

note: City of Mountain Lake campground at Golf Course Road and Prince Street: pull-through sites in rows between tree lines, with fire rings and picnic tables, beside a city park with a playground, the golf course, disc golf and a 5.25-mile paved trail (rental bikes on site). Big rigs welcome. --Claude
summary: City page read: $35/night ($600 monthly, $2,000 seasonal), first come first served, May 1 - Oct 1, full hookups (amps not stated), shower house, flush toilets, dump. 17 vs 18 sites conflict on the same page (left at 18). Not waterfront kept.
flags: Site count: the same city page says 'The seventeen camping site are available on a first come, first serve basis' and, in its listing paragraph, '18 RV/trailer sites, pull-thrus'. Imagery shows two rows of pull-throughs (roughly 9 + 9). sites.count 18 left as stored.

The page's opening notice is dated: 'open to all recreational, seasonal, and critical worker campers on May 1, 2025' (pandemic-era wording). Season May 1 - Oct 1 is also in the seasonal-rate line, so written; no 2026 notice posted.
Long-stay: monthly ($600) and seasonal ($2,000) rates are offered, but nightly first-come camping is the stated standard; public city campground, keep.

Website: the stored https://mountainlakemn.com/business/island-view-campground/ serves the city page; the canonical address is https://cityofmountainlakemn.gov/business/island-view-campground/ (apply.py does not write websites). Phone 507-427-2999 (City Hall) matches.

Waterfront: keep not waterfront. Imagery: the site rows sit between tree lines south of a gravel lane; the nearest water (the lake's south arm/pond to the north) is ~200 m away behind woods, with houses to the west.
